bull.b: CAVA has delivered substantial multi-year revenue expansion while moving into sustained profitability. This indicates growing brand reach and customer demand, giving the company a stronger base from which to fund restaurant openings, improve scale economics, and build earnings power over the next several quarters.

Positive traffic growth alongside strong comparable sales suggests demand is broad-based rather than dependent only on new locations. High new-unit productivity and continued openings can extend the company’s growth runway, increase brand presence, and support recurring revenue expansion over time.

A sizable liquidity position and positive operating cash flow provide financial flexibility to support restaurant development, technology, and operating investments. Access to additional committed funding also reduces reliance on external capital while the company scales its restaurant base.

bear.b: Rising food, packaging, and labor costs are already reducing restaurant-level margin, while management expects further cost increases. If pricing and productivity do not fully offset these pressures, operating leverage from strong sales growth may translate less efficiently into sustained earnings.

Although operations generate positive cash, relatively small free cash flow means a limited portion of reported earnings remains after investment needs. Continued expansion could keep conversion under pressure, reducing internally available funds for reinvestment, buybacks, or resilience during weaker trading periods.

The increase in absolute debt adds fixed financial obligations as CAVA expands, even though the balance sheet has improved to positive equity. Modest recent returns on equity indicate that growth has not yet consistently translated into strong owner returns, limiting the quality of earnings expansion.
